meta.title: The Map Without a Key
meta.textType: story: a school map for a pen pal

paragraphs: On Thursday, October fifteenth, at four o'clock, Leo came to Lily's house. They sat at the kitchen table, and Leo opened Lily's laptop. He wanted to read an email from his pen pal, Ravi. Pip lay under the table with his red ball.

The screen showed Ravi's email. "Dear Leo, thank you for the photo of your school. Where is your library, and where is your gym? Please draw a map to show me the way. Best wishes, Ravi." "That is easy," said Leo. "I know where everything is."

Leo took a clean sheet of paper and drew a map of the school. He drew a book, a circle, a ball, and some squares. "The gym is north of the field," he said. "The library is opposite the gym, and the classrooms are close to the library." Lily looked at the drawing. "The book is the library, isn't it?" she asked. "Yes, it is," said Leo.

Then Tom came into the kitchen for a glass of water. He looked at the map over Lily's shoulder. "Which one is the library?" he asked. "You have mixed up the gym and the library, haven't you?" "No, I haven't!" said Leo. "The book is the library." "I can't see that on the map," said Tom. "Ravi is far away, and he cannot ask you," said Lily. "A map needs a key."

Leo copied the map on a new sheet with the same shapes. Then he wrote the key clearly at the bottom. The key said, "Book: library. Circle: gym. Ball: field. Square: classroom." Tom looked at the new map again. "Now I know exactly where the gym is," he said. "I hope Ravi can read it now," said Leo. Leo took a photo of the map and sent it to Ravi. Ravi answered soon. A new email came, and Leo was glad. "Dear Leo, now I can find your library! Thank you for the map. Best wishes, Ravi." Lily smiled and said, "A good map always has a key." Pip dropped his red ball at Leo's feet.
